events.subtitle: RESISTANCE Album Release
events.category: Afro-Caribbean jazz / tenor trio / album release
events.factual_description: The Jazz Gallery presents Jacques Schwarz-Bart's RESISTANCE Album Release on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, with sets at 7:00 PM and 9:00 PM. The announced live trio is Schwarz-Bart on tenor saxophone, Or Bareket on bass and Ele Howell on drums. The venue describes Schwarz-Bart as a Guadeloupe-born pioneer of Gwoka jazz and Voodoo jazz whose work engages Afro-Caribbean traditions, spirituality and collective memory. Quai Son Records describes Resistance as a tenor-saxophone, bass and drums project that deliberately omits piano and guitar to create open improvisational space; the recording itself features Reggie Washington on bass and Arnaud Dolmen on drums, so those studio personnel are not represented as members of the September 30 live trio. The full ten-track album was released on August 28, 2026. General seating is $33 and cabaret seating is $38.50, with lower member/student prices also published; livestream access is $22.

en.why_it_matters: Resistance is built around what is missing as much as what is present: tenor saxophone, bass and drums with no piano or guitar to lock the harmony down. Schwarz-Bart brings his Guadeloupean and Afro-Caribbean rhythmic language into that open space, and the New York release date reshapes the project around Bareket and Howell rather than simply reproducing the recording trio. That combination of instrumental identity, memory and improvisational room is enough to make this more than a routine club set.
en.trip_verdict: If New York is already in play that Wednesday, The Jazz Gallery is a worthwhile way to spend the evening and either set works. From the DMV, I would fold it into a broader New York trip rather than travel solely for this album-cycle date.

es.why_it_matters: Resistance se construye tanto alrededor de lo que falta como de lo que está presente: sax tenor, bajo y batería, sin piano ni guitarra que amarren la armonía. Schwarz-Bart lleva su lenguaje rítmico guadalupeño y afrocaribeño a ese espacio abierto, y la fecha de lanzamiento en Nueva York rehace el proyecto con Bareket y Howell en vez de limitarse a reproducir el trío del disco. Esa mezcla de identidad instrumental, memoria y libertad improvisatoria basta para que sea mucho más que otra fecha de club.
es.trip_verdict: Si Nueva York ya está en juego ese miércoles, The Jazz Gallery vale perfectamente la noche y cualquiera de los dos sets funciona. Desde el DMV, lo integraría a un viaje más amplio a Nueva York en vez de subir exclusivamente por esta fecha del ciclo de lanzamiento.
